raw_response:
I’m 60 this year, and I’ve been working these 6 mu for twenty years. Just me and the wife now—our children have gone to the city. I only finished primary school, so I don’t read many books, but I know my own fields. I watch what Old Wang and the others in the village do, and I stick with what has put food on the table.

My 6 mu are split up like this. I’ve got 2 mu where I plant spring cabbage around early March. I buy improved seed from the shop in town—about 30 yuan per mu. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer on that land before planting, that’s roughly what they call 20 kg of nitrogen per mu I suppose, plus some phosphorus and potassium. I till it with the small tiller I bought five years ago. I irrigate three times from the well: right after planting, when the heads start forming, and once more if the weather turns dry in May. I pull the weeds by hand, me and the wife. We don’t spray much pesticide on cabbage—if I see worms, I hit them with what the shop recommends, maybe once or twice. I expect about 3,000 kg per mu if the weather is fair, same as last year.

After I cut that spring cabbage in mid-June, I turn that same 2 mu over to chinesecabbage. The turnaround is tight, only a few days. I don’t have time for deep tillage, just a quick pass with the tiller and I plant right away in late June. Chinesecabbage needs feeding, so I put down another two bags of compound fertilizer per mu, maybe a little more urea than for regular cabbage because it grows fast in summer. I irrigate four times—July and August are hot and dry here. I expect about 4,000 kg per mu by October if the price holds.

Then I have another 2 mu for fall cabbage. I plant that in late July after the wheat would have come off, but I don’t grow wheat—too much work for just two of us. Fall cabbage gets the same treatment: two bags of compound fertilizer per mu, three irrigations, and I expect about 3,500 kg per mu by November.

On the remaining 2 mu—wait, that’s already 4 mu. Let me think again. I have 6 mu total. The first 2 mu do spring cabbage then chinesecabbage. That leaves 4 mu. On 2 mu I plant chili in late April. Chili is tricky, but the price was good last year. I use one bag of compound fertilizer per mu and topdress with a bit of urea when it flowers. I irrigate three times. I expect about 800 kg per mu of fresh chili. The other 2 mu I plant kidney bean in early May. Beans don’t need much nitrogen, so I only use half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, mainly for the phosphorus. I irrigate twice. I expect about 1,000 kg per mu.

Labor is tight. It’s just me and the wife, and my back isn’t what it used to be. Spring cabbage and chili planting happen at the same time, so we’re rushing. We don’t hire labor unless we absolutely have to—it’s 120 yuan per day now, too expensive. Family labor is about 60 days for me and 40 days for the wife across the whole year.

Money is always tight. Seed, fertilizer, and pumping water will cost me about 3,800 yuan total this year. I’d like to put down more fertilizer, but I need to keep some cash in case the wife needs medicine or the pump breaks. Better to under-fertilize a little than to have no money in hand.
